_readme: Single source of truth for the per-service deploy contract.
Consumed by the shared release workflow (.github/workflows/release-service.yml,
called by wrapper, B2B-CRM and zopkit-lens) and by ecs/deploy-service.sh, the
local operator path. Both read THIS file, so the per-service contract cannot
drift between them the way it did when each carried its own copy as a bash
`case` -- the script skipped build+push for an existing immutable tag so a
rollback worked, while the CI copy still rebuilt and died on the re-push.
Fields:
app           app key, matches local.apps in the terraform stack
ecr           ECR repository name (NOT environment-prefixed; images are shared
across environments and promoted, never rebuilt per env)
source_repo   owner/repo holding the Dockerfile. "" means this repo (wrapper),
which is also what makes CI build it here rather than expect an
image already pushed by a sibling repo.
repo_env      deploy.env variable holding the LOCAL checkout path, for the
operator script only.
dockerfile    path to the Dockerfile, relative to the source checkout root
context       docker build context, relative to the source checkout root
target        multi-stage build target
migrate       run DB migrations as a one-off task after the release. Only the
service that OWNS the schema does this; siblings share its DB.
migrate_cmd   container command override for that one-off task
api_subdomain host label for the smoke test; null for headless workers.
Full URL = https://<api_subdomain>.<root_domain><health_path>
root_domain is staging.zopkit.com or zopkit.com, so the same
entry serves both environments.
health_path   path for the smoke test; null for headless workers
sibling       service that rides this one's release (same image, no migrate).
Deployed in the SAME run: two dispatches racing the shared
deploy-queue got the older one cancelled and left the worker a
source_ref    branch the app ships from, when it is not the default. academy
deploys from `dev`, not `main`.
version behind.
NOT YET ONBOARDED -- these run in staging but exist in neither deploy
path, so they are released by hand (see the Deployment-Manager IAM user in
CloudTrail). Adding one means one entry here, once the source repo, Dockerfile
path and health endpoint are confirmed:
ops-web               ecr/repo/health TBC
entertainment-erp-web ecr/repo/health TBC
CONFLICT — academy-web is deployed by its OWN pipeline today:
Zopkit/Zopkit-Academy .github/workflows/deploy-dev-ecs.yml (branch `dev`)
OIDC role zopkit-staging-academy-github-deploy, builds Dockerfile.backend from
the repo root, registers a task definition from taskdef.json and calls
update-service directly — bypassing terraform. It also ships the SPA to
zopkit-staging-academy-fe and invalidates CloudFront E1BG5TRQBP57TT.
Now that academy-web IS terraform-managed, that pipeline and terraform both
own the task definition, so every academy deploy creates drift. Pick one owner
before routing academy through this manifest.

lens-web migrates from the GitHub runner (pnpm db:migrate against DATABASE_URL), not as an ECS task -- its image does not ship the drizzle meta/_journal.json, so a container-side migrate exits 1. migrate is false here and lens's own workflow runs its migration step BEFORE calling the shared release.
FRONTENDS -- the `frontends` block feeds .github/workflows/publish-spa.yml, the
shared S3+CloudFront publish. Each app repo still BUILDS its own SPA (different
package managers, node versions and baked VITE_* env) and uploads dist as an
artifact; only the publish half is shared. no_cache lists the files served with
no-cache -- everything else gets the immutable one-year header, so a file missing
from this list is a file browsers will pin for a year.
wrapper's only frontend environment is PROD: a push to its main releases the API
to staging while shipping the SPA to app.zopkit.com. That split predates this
manifest and is recorded here rather than hidden.
